role: Agentic-first web stack: communication, execution, and coordination framed around tokens, tools, capabilities, traces, and swarms.

capabilities.name: GET /health
capabilities.description: Liveness. Declared unauthenticated.

capabilities.name: GET /ready
capabilities.description: Readiness. Declared unauthenticated.

capabilities.name: GET /metrics
capabilities.description: Prometheus metrics.

capabilities.name: GET /v1/agentic/capabilities

capabilities.name: GET /v1/agentic/codecs

capabilities.name: GET /v1/names/providers

capabilities.name: GET /v1/names/endpoints

capabilities.name: POST /api/sessions/{id}/search
capabilities.description: Search within the session's page.

capabilities.name: GET /api/sessions/{id}/ping
capabilities.description: Session keepalive.

capabilities.name: POST /api/sessions/{id}/execute
capabilities.description: Execute script in the session -- arbitrary code in a live browser context.

capabilities.description: Parse a document the caller supplies.

capabilities.name: GET /v1/names/crawl
capabilities.description: Crawl registered endpoints. Reaches out across the network.

note: requires_grant is derived from the gateway's own auth middleware, which is a total rule rather than a per-route annotation: is_unauthenticated_path admits only /health, /ready and the documentation paths, and every other route is refused without a bearer token. So the field carries little information here -- eighteen of twenty routes require a grant because SPINE authenticates by default. That is the correct reading of its design, not a gap in this manifest. SPINE has no scopes. A token that can read a session can also execute script in it, and requires_grant cannot express a distinction the gateway does not draw. If per-route scopes are ever added, this file gains real signal; until then the honest summary is authenticated or not. budgeted is judged here and marks the routes whose cost is set by what the caller sends or asks the gateway to reach: embeddings scales with the submitted text, parse and compile with the submitted document, navigate and crawl fetch whatever the caller names, session creation holds a live browser context, and execute runs arbitrary script in one. /metrics is left granted-and-unbudgeted as declared, though it is worth noting it is authenticated while conventionally it is the endpoint operators scrape.
